canonical_topic: Investing in redundant compressors to grow firm-contract capacity
definition: A worked example showing how a pipeline with unreliable compressors can increase profit by adding backup compressors, allowing it to safely sell more firm (vs. interruptible) capacity.
core_idea: Because firm-contract nondelivery penalties vastly exceed firm-contract delivery revenue, a pipeline's profit is highly sensitive to reliability; investing in redundant compressors to raise reliability lets the pipeline sell more high-margin firm capacity instead of low-margin interruptible capacity, sharply increasing profit even after higher maintenance costs.
key_points: Setup: 5 compressor stations in series, each up 85% of the time (1 week/year scheduled maintenance). The pipeline can tolerate a single down compressor (losing 20% capacity per offline unit) but fails when two adjacent compressors are down simultaneously.
Pricing: firm transportation pays $1/MMBtu delivered but costs the pipeline $12.50/MMBtu if undelivered; interruptible transportation pays $0.15/MMBtu delivered and costs nothing if undelivered.

Baseline: the pipeline was unable to operate at all 8% of days and ran at full capacity only 42.5% of the time; with 60% of capacity sold as firm and 91.7% of firm volume actually delivered, nondelivery penalties consumed essentially all the profit from delivered firm volume.
Strategy: add a second (mostly idle) compressor at each station to raise overall pipeline reliability, which allows more capacity to be safely sold as firm rather than interruptible.
Result: capacity generating $0.15 on 40% utilization shifted to capacity generating $1 on 80% utilization, roughly a 100x increase in profit, which more than offset doubled maintenance costs.
relationships: Firm/interruptible pricing asymmetry ties directly to the buyer-seller firm vs. interruptible contract distinction.
trading_implications: Reliability investment can be evaluated as a real option: it converts low-margin interruptible sales into high-margin firm sales by shrinking the tail risk of nondelivery penalties.
Because nondelivery penalties are far larger than delivery revenue for firm contracts, small improvements in operating reliability can produce outsized profit swings.
caveats: It may look wasteful to add a compressor that is idle most of the time, but its value comes from reliability/optionality, not utilization.
